items.why: Both rules are stated: chloroform as an ingredient makes a cosmetic adulterated, and processing-solvent residue is not an ingredient. But the answer then says the sources cannot settle whether the cream is adulterated, even though 700.18(b) (in the evidence) answers it, so R3 is missing. ce 0 because the adulteration statement is cited to 700.18(a), but it is in (b); there are no [n] markers, the 301/601(a) basis is not given, and 'as a byproduct' drops 'from the synthesis of an ingredient'.

Same prose as the other item, plus the verbatim 700.18(a)/(b) text with correct [1]/[2] markers, so R1 (with 301/601(a)) and R2 are present. It still says the sources cannot decide whether the cream is adulterated, although (b) answers it (R3 missing). ce 0 because the prose cites 700.18(a) for the adulteration statement, which is in (b).

740.12(a) (the definition covers sprays for 'use all over the body'), (b) (the label must bear a statement) and (c) (the hygiene/medical-word ban) are restated correctly, with correct markers. It never concludes that this spray is a feminine deodorant spray or that its label needs the caution, so R1/R2 are only quoted, not applied. Leaving out the caution wording is not held against it, since that text is not in the stored regulation.

It states the 720.4(e) rule (each shade for (c)(6) hair colouring; one form for shades differing only in colour additive) and the (d) ordering and naming hierarchy. But it never applies them (12 hair-dye statements, one lipstick form), never mentions (c)(7)/lipstick, and ends with a wrongful 'not enough information' decline even though (e) answers the question. ce 0: the (d)(1)-(3) contents are each assigned to the wrong subparagraph, (d)(3) is garbled, and (c)(6)(i)-(viii) are wrongly said to state that items 'must be listed as per (d)' (unsupported); the fragrance-withholding condition is also dropped.

Same prose as the other item, but with no verbatim snippet and no markers. It states the 720.4(e) shade rule and the (d) ordering and naming, but does not apply them to 12 hair-dye shades vs one lipstick form, omits (c)(7), and wrongly declines although (e) was in the evidence. ce 0 for the mis-numbered (d)(1)-(3) attributions; the claim that (c)(6)(i)-(viii) 'must be listed as per (d)' is unsupported.

70.3(s) (includes the eyebrow and the skin below it), (u) (coal-tar hair dye exemption conditioned on the statutory caution and patch-test directions, not for non-coal-tar colourants) and (v) (excludes lips and mucous membranes) are correct and correctly cited. It does not explicitly conclude that the brow tint is eye-area use or that lip gloss is not externally applied (R1/R2 quoted, not applied); it drops 'conspicuously'/'adequate' and the diluent limit.

The answer gives the correct rate ($0.45 per pound, $288 minimum) and payment method from 80.10(d), citing (a) and (d) correctly. R1 is marked absent because it never works out the $900 for a 2,000-pound batch. It also leaves out the 80.10(c) advance-deposit option (R3) and the CFSAN mailing address, although (c) was in the evidence.

Mixed case: the answer correctly paraphrases 73.2725(a)-(e) with accurate inline citations (no [n] markers), including the 70.25 labeling rule (R2). It also states the exemption from certification. It never draws the 'yes, you may use it in the eye shadow' conclusion (R1 absent) and ends by saying the sources are insufficient, which undercuts the answer, although all five paragraphs were in the evidence.

Mixed case: the answer correctly paraphrases 73.2725(a)-(e), covering the 70.25 labeling rule (R2) and the certification exemption (R3), and adds a verbatim excerpt of (a)-(c) whose markers point to the right paragraphs. It never draws the 'yes, permitted for eye shadow' conclusion (R1 absent) and still ends with an 'insufficient information' statement, although the evidence fully supported an answer.

All key provisions are stated correctly with correct markers: 74.2317(b) GMP-amount use, (c) labeling per 70.25, (d) certification of all batches under part 80, and the 70.3(v) definition. R1 and R2 are marked absent because the answer only quotes. It never concludes that the body butter qualifies as externally applied, that use is permitted, or that there is no numeric limit.

The answer correctly states that cosmetics containing halogenated salicylanilides are adulterated (700.15(b)) and that such products in interstate commerce after 1 December 1975 face regulatory action (R2). It drops 'at any level for any purpose' and section 601(a), and never says 'No'. It then says the sources cannot settle whether 0.25% may be sold, which misleadingly implies the level matters, although (b) was in the evidence and answers the question outright.

The paraphrase correctly gives the adulteration rule (b) and the post-1 December 1975 regulatory-action rule (R2). The appended verbatim 700.15 text, with correct markers, does include 'at any level for any purpose ... section 601(a)'. The answer still never concludes 'No' (R1 absent) and says the sources cannot settle whether 0.25% may be sold. That contradicts the text it quotes and could mislead the user.

verdicts.lens: RUBRIC, CHECKLIST AND FABRICATION: every rubric field and checklist status re-derived from the key, the answer text, the MARKERS and the EVIDENCE, looking for invented requirements, wrong citations, misapplied provisions and critical errors

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The prose says 700.18(a) makes a chloroform-ingredient cosmetic adulterated, but (a) only says chloroform 'may render injurious'; the adulteration rule is in (b), so ce is 0. R1 is right in substance but lacks 301/601(a). R2 is present, though 'as a byproduct' drops 'from the synthesis of an ingredient', so conditions are partly kept. R3 is absent because the answer declines although (b) was in the evidence. No critical error: it never says the cream is adulterated or that the exemption fails. Nothing is invented, so fab is 0. sub 1 and comp 2 hold because (b) is fully surfaced but the decline could mislead.

Confirmed. It repeats the same prose, which wrongly attributes the adulteration rule to (a), so ce is 0. The appended verbatim (a)/(b) has correct [1]/[2] markers, so citation_support is yes, and it supplies 301/601(a) and the full residue exception (R1 and R2 present). R3 is absent because it still says the sources cannot decide, contradicting the (b) text it quotes. No critical error and nothing fabricated. sub 1, comp 2 and conditions partly are supported.

Confirmed. The (a), (b) and (c) restatements match the evidence, and each [n] marker points to the paragraph it summarises, so ce is 1 and citation_support is yes. The answer never concludes that this all-over-body spray is a feminine deodorant spray or that its label needs the statement, so R1 and R2 are only quoted and count as absent. R3 is present. It invents no caution wording, so there is no critical error and fab is 0. The missing caution text is excluded by the key. sub 2 and comp 2 hold: nothing is misstated and (a) and (b) are surfaced.

Confirmed. The (d)(1)-(3) contents are each shifted one paragraph and (d)(3) is garbled, so ce is 0. The claim that (c)(6)(i)-(viii) 'must be listed as per (d)' is unsupported: those paragraphs are bare category names. This is a misattribution plus a should-to-must upgrade, which belongs under sub, not fab, because (d) does govern all listings. The (e) shade rule is stated correctly but never applied to 12 statements and one lipstick form, so R1 and R2 are absent. (c)(7) is omitted, so comp is 1. R3 and R4 are present, though 'except fragrance/flavor' drops the supplier-refusal condition, so conditions are partly kept. The final decline is inappropriate because (e) was in the evidence. The verbatim [1]-[3] markers are correct, so citation_support is yes. No critical error.

Confirmed. It has the same prose as the other item without the verbatim snippet or markers, so citation_support is na. The mis-numbered (d)(1)-(3) attributions give ce 0. The (c)(6) 'must be listed as per (d)' claims are unsupported attributions, not fabrication. R1 and R2 are absent because the rule is never applied and (c)(7) is missing. R3 and R4 are present. The decline is inappropriate. sub 1 and comp 1 hold.

Confirmed. (s) correctly includes the eyebrow and the skin below it, (v) excludes lips and mucous membranes, and (u) keeps the coal-tar limit and the caution and patch-test label condition, all with correct markers, so ce is 1 and citation_support is yes. It never applies them to the brow tint or the lip gloss, so R1 and R2 are absent. R3 is present, losing only 'conspicuously'/'adequate' and the 601(a) reference. That keeps the substance of the condition and does not make the exemption unconditional, so there is no critical error. sub 2, comp 2 and conditions yes are defensible. Unlike the 20 Oct calibration answer, this one keeps both the eyebrow and the patch-test condition.

Confirmed. $0.45 per pound with a $288 minimum is correctly cited to (a), and the payment method (money order, bank draft or certified check to FDA, collectible at par at Washington, DC) is correctly cited to (d), so R2 is present and ce is 1. The 80.21(j)(1)-(2) cross-reference is copied from (a), not invented. The fee for this batch ($900) is never worked out, so R1 is absent. The (c) advance-deposit option and the CFSAN forwarding address are omitted although they were in the evidence, so R3 is absent and comp is 1. There is a minor oddity: the marker [1] after the question heading 'How do we pay...' points to (a), but a question makes no claim. No critical error and nothing fabricated.

The checklist is wrong on R3. The answer states '73.2725(e): ... batches thereof are exempt from certification pursuant to section 721(c)', which is exactly R3 and needs no further application. The scorer's own 'why' says it 'also states the exemption from certification', and the identical prose in #Y is marked R3 present. All other fields hold: the inline (a)-(e) citations are correct (ce 1), no markers (citation_support na), R1 absent because it never says 'yes' for the eye shadow, R2 present, sub 1 because of the misleading final 'not enough information' line, comp 2, declined true and decline_appropriate no.

Confirmed. The (a)-(e) paraphrase is accurate and correctly cited, and the appended verbatim (a)-(c) has correct [1]-[3] markers. R2 (70.25 labeling) and R3 (exempt from 721(c) certification) are present. R1 is absent because it never concludes 'yes, permitted in the eye shadow'. It ends with an inappropriate 'insufficient information' line although all five paragraphs were in the evidence. The missing spec values are excluded by the key. No critical error and nothing fabricated.

Confirmed. 74.2317(b), (c) and (d) and 70.3(v) are restated accurately with correct markers (ce 1, citation_support yes). R3 (certify all batches under part 80) and R4 (70.25 label) are present. R1 is absent because it never concludes that the body butter is externally applied and the use permitted. R2 is absent because it never says there is no numeric limit, only quoting 'GMP amounts'. No numeric limit is invented and certification is not denied, so there is no critical error. sub 2 and comp 2 hold.

Confirmed. The inline citations to (a), (b) and (c) match their contents (ce 1, no markers, so citation_support na). R2 (regulatory action after 1 December 1975) is present. R1 is absent: the answer drops 'at any level for any purpose' and 601(a), never says 'No', and then says the sources cannot settle whether 0.25% can be sold. That decline implies the level might matter, but it does not state that a threshold exists, so it falls just short of the critical error. Dropping the any-level limit, the crux of the question, supports comp 1, conditions partly and sub 1. Nothing is fabricated.

Confirmed. It has the same prose plus the verbatim 700.15 text with correct [1]-[3] markers, which supplies 'at any level for any purpose ... section 601(a)' (comp 2, citation_support yes). R2 is present. R1 is absent because it never concludes 'No', and the closing decline contradicts the quoted (b), so sub 1 and conditions partly hold. No threshold is asserted and nothing is fabricated.
